plan.topic: Is plague curable? Common antibiotics work well when started early, which corrects the 'no cure' myth
plan.angle: Attributed myth correction. Hook: 'Is there a cure for plague? Yes. CDC says common antibiotics treat it.' Then the honest part: timing matters most for pneumonic plague. CDC and WHO say untreated pneumonic plague is very often fatal, and prompt treatment greatly improves survival. Use the agencies' wording and figures exactly, with no invented percentages. Health authorities can give close contacts preventive antibiotics. No drug names with doses, no stockpiling or self-treatment. Possible exposure plus fever or cough means contacting a doctor or local health authority urgently. Close with the line 'if you're worried, talk to a health professional'. 35–50s.

package.title: Is Plague Curable? What CDC and WHO Actually Say #shorts
package.description:
Yes, plague is curable with antibiotics. CDC says treatment must start quickly, and WHO says antibiotics are effective if plague is diagnosed in time. WHO: untreated pneumonic plague can be fatal within 18–24 hours, and recovery rates are high if treated within 24 hours of symptoms.
Don't stockpile or self-treat. Possible exposure plus fever, cough or trouble breathing? Contact a doctor or local health authority urgently. If you're worried, talk to a health professional.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation.

Sources:
WHO Plague fact sheet: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/plague
CDC About Plague: https://www.cdc.gov/plague/about/index.html

script.hook_pattern: A search-question hook with an attributed myth correction. In the first 2 seconds the viewer gets the question, a quick 'Yes' and the named agency (CDC), with CDC's timing condition attached ('treatment must start quickly'). WHO then corrects the 'no cure' myth. Next comes the honest catch about timing and the pneumonic form, using WHO's actual wording ('can be fatal within 18 to 24 hours' if left untreated). Then comes the payoff: WHO's 24-hour recovery line, followed by preventive antibiotics for close contacts and the urgent-care line (fever, cough or trouble breathing). It ends with the reassuring close, which loops back to the opening question.

factcheck.summary:
I checked all five sources against the live pages, and each one exists and says what the script uses it for. CDC's About Plague page (last reviewed Aug 24, 2026) says "Plague can be cured with antibiotics, but treatment must be given quickly", which supports s1. The WHO fact sheet (published 29 Sep 2026) says antibiotics "are effective against plague if patients are diagnosed in time", which supports s2. It also says "recovery rates are high if detected and treated in time (within 24 hours of onset of symptoms)", which supports s4. And it says close contacts of pneumonic plague patients get "seven-day chemoprophylaxis", which supports s5. That scene is also backed by MMWR RR 70(3), 2021, and CDC's Clinical Care page (last reviewed May 15, 2024): both recommend preventive antibiotics after close (<6 ft), sustained contact. CDC's Signs and Symptoms page lists fever and cough among pneumonic plague symptoms and says "seek immediate medical attention", which supports s6.

Safety is handled well. There's no dosing, no drug names and no self-treatment, there's an explicit line against stockpiling and self-treating, and the line "If you're worried, talk to a health professional" is there. The Irkutsk teaser makes no status claims, so it doesn't need a date. There's no fear framing, and the title pays off its question.

The only problem is minor. s3 is a paraphrase, but the hook plan says it uses "WHO's exact wording". WHO's actual line is "can be fatal within 18 to 24 hours of disease onset if left untreated." I've given a fix that uses the real wording, which is also more concrete. Two other scenes could be tighter, but neither needs a change: s6 could also name breathing symptoms, and s7 carries no factual claims.

issues.claim: WHO says pneumonic plague, the lung form, can be fatal if it isn't diagnosed and treated early.
issues.problem: This is a paraphrase, but the hook plan says it uses WHO's exact wording. The WHO fact sheet actually says: 'Pneumonic plague can be fatal within 18 to 24 hours of disease onset if left untreated.' The meaning is close, but the attribution should match the source, and the real wording has a concrete timeframe.
issues.fix: Narration: "But here's the catch: timing. WHO says untreated pneumonic plague, the lung form, can be fatal within 18 to 24 hours." On-screen text: "Pneumonic: treat early (WHO)"

issues.claim: Possible exposure plus fever or cough? Contact a doctor or local health authority urgently.
issues.problem: This is accurate, but CDC's symptom list for pneumonic plague also includes shortness of breath and chest pain, and CDC says to 'seek immediate medical attention'. As written, the line names only 2 of the warning signs. This is optional wording polish.
issues.fix: Narration: "Don't stockpile or self-treat. Possible exposure plus fever, cough or trouble breathing? Contact a doctor or local health authority urgently." List item: "Possible exposure + fever, cough or breathlessness: call a doctor now"

notes: At ~5.8s a small floating 'Antibiotics' label sits directly on top of the caption pill, clashing with 'TO START QUICKLY.' — matches the automated overlap finding at t=5.84.
At ~17.8s and ~21.8s the caption text overlaps the lungs/body artwork — matches automated overlap findings at t=17.82 and t=21.84 ('Timing. WHO says untreated' and 'within 18 to 24 hours').

At ~50.2s the caption shows the word 'CONFIRMED' at the start of the line before 'ABOUT THE IRKUTSK CASE?', which can read as a standalone claim that the case is confirmed — conflicts with the brand rule to always pair 'confirmed' with 'reported/suspected' status on screen.

audio.soundNotes: Music sits at a good -13.5 dB under voice; small +1.3 dB nudge lifts it in the pauses toward target without breaking the under-voice ceiling. Thinned the dense SFX cluster around the "Within 24h" reveal (three overlapping transition sounds were 7-12 dB too hot during speech) and the "chips" transition cluster at ~36.3-37.4s, which had up to 9 stacked hits in just over a second; kept the lead transition hit and one supporting swoosh, dropped the redundant blips/swooshes, and softened one overly loud blip at 10.85s. Added three bespoke, restrained cues (a grounded heartbeat pulse on open, a breath/wheeze for the lungs visual, a crisp chime on the 24-hour stat) to add felt texture without competing with narration.
